project.name: Beta 2 · layered
project.title: Beta 2 · layered: plates that host the train
project.blurb: Two Ø19 discs on Dual_Dial_Concept's dial centres, the movement centred on them, set by a crown at 3 o'clock on the movement, between the swivel lugs. The crown's worm turns a small crown arbor whose wheel turns the minute pinion; a transfer arbor under the minute disc lets both intermediates sit exactly on the centre line: minute pinion 12 → 18, pinion 11 → 22, pinion 11 → 22, pinion 13 → hour wheel 26 (exactly 12:1), so the discs keep true time against each other and turn the same way. 10 crown turns an hour. Module 0.6, black delrin, brass rods. Plates in layers, each hosting the wheels at its own heights: the 3/8" main plate high on the hour side and stepped down on the minute side; a 1/8" secondary plate on that step, the cradle that holds the stem down, carries the crown, transfer and minute arbors and gives every top-layer wheel one unbroken floor; a 1/8" transfer plate along the south and east walls whose twin arms carry the first intermediate down from a round anchor foot; a 1/8" NE plate; and the hour side's top plate, all flush with the discs. Movement 45.5 x 32.4 mm, 11.11 mm from the back of the main plate to the top of the discs.
source: Claude, 2026-11-23, from Adam's brief: the watch version of Hemistitch, hand-set, discs centred on the movement, crown at 3 o'clock on the movement to clear the hinged lugs, standard movement layering with the guts on show, a reliable machining tolerance; the case scaled to fit afterwards. Layout from a search over every rod, bearing, gear layer, the worm and the stem, scored on the box centred on the discs.

Layered plates: Claude, 2026-11-24, from Adam's modification lists on Beta 2 · haute, then his 19 markup notes and sketches K55 and K56 (the cradle, no breaks under wheels, the anchor merge, no ledges).

rules.why: module 0.6: the 0.5 mm end mill has room in every tooth space

shop.note: black delrin throughout; fits are delrin placeholders until the press-fit test

arbors.name: Minute arbor
arbors.role: Turns once an hour; the minute disc sits right on its 12-tooth pinion, which takes the crown (from E's wheel) and drives the transfer arbor. Runs in plain delrin holes (under the disc), so the worm can lie close beside its rod. A collar under the back face keeps it from lifting out.

arbors.name: Transfer arbor (B)
arbors.role: Under the minute disc's lower edge: its wheel is driven by the minute pinion and turns on the secondary plate's floor; its pinion drives the first intermediate. Pivots: a bearing in the main plate, the secondary plate under its wheel.

arbors.name: First intermediate

partNames.a1: First intermediate wheel and pinion (one piece, 1/8" delrin)

arbors.role: On the centre line. Its 22-tooth wheel is driven by the transfer pinion; its 11-tooth pinion drives the second intermediate. One piece of 1/8" delrin, deep in the main plate (bearing below), its top pivot in the transfer plate's pad on twin arms.

arbors.name: Second intermediate

partNames.a2: Second intermediate wheel and pinion (one piece, 1/8" delrin)

arbors.role: On the centre line, north of A1. Its 22-tooth wheel, 0.3 over A1's wheel, is driven by A1's pinion; its 13-tooth pinion drives the hour wheel. One piece of 1/8" delrin; one bearing down on A1's floor (P27), its top pivot in the top plate's pad on twin arms.

arbors.name: Hour arbor
arbors.role: Turns once in 12 hours; its wheel runs low in the main plate (under the first intermediate's pinion level), the hour disc pressed on its rod above.

arbors.name: Crown arbor (E)
arbors.role: Takes the crown: the worm on the stem turns its 15-tooth worm wheel (in a pocket in the lower plate), and its 18-tooth wheel turns the minute pinion. Runs in plain delrin holes. One crown turn = one tooth: 10 turns an hour.

hands.name: Hour disc
hands.role: Ø19 black delrin, numerals V-carved and filled; on the hour rod at the minute disc's height, just above the hour wheel. Turns the same way as the minute disc (four reductions).

hands.name: Minute disc
hands.role: Ø19 black delrin, V-carved and filled; sits right on the minute pinion.

plate.name: Bench
plate.role: Just the bench under the movement; the plates are the drawn parts.
